# dsh-superagent
> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of
our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat i
t as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style a
nd engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own enviro

nment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the
implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*.
Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented
ssed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.
This repository is a fork of deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype. It keeps the upstream design and
adds the changes under Fork notes.
dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepS
eek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for w
ork, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the or
iginal conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.
It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as
much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's atte
ntion, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when some
one must act or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of
or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.
## Install
dsh-superagent is a DSH bundle: `dsh plugin` installs it into one profile, next to the plugins that
profile already loads.

- DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2 or later. The desktop app 0.2.1-rc.5 is known to work.
- `gh` 2.48
or later and `git` 2.32 or later on `PATH`: the GitHub Source calls `gh`, and ticket checkouts use `

git`.
- Optional, only for the Feishu Source: `lark-cli` and a Feishu or Lark app with a bot.
Node.js 22.19+ or 24+ is needed only when you build from source; the release tarball ships the built

Restart that profile — quit and reopen the desktop app, or restart `dsh web` — then choose **Superag
ent** in the sidebar.
The bundle ships a default state directory, `<DSH_HOME>/state/dsh-superagent`, for its database, loc
ks, worker shims and ticket directories. To keep it elsewhere, add this to the profile's `cordis.pat

`stateDir` cannot change after the first start.
### Configure it
Open **Superagent** and fill in:
1. **Sources → GitHub**: the repository as `owner/name`, and the `gh` CLI the agent acts as. The age
nt comments, pushes and opens pull requests as that account, so it needs write access; a dedicated a

ccount keeps its work distinguishable from yours.
2. **Policy**: the GitHub logins allowed to ask fo

r work. Until the list has someone, no request can become a ticket.
3. **Execution**: the ticket dir
ectory root and a `prepare` command that gives each ticket its own checkout, for example a `git work
tree` of a local clone.
Then ask for work from an allowed account: open an Issue or comment on one, mentioning the agent, fo
r example `@<agent-login> fix the typo in the README`. With shared-account mode, the comment must *s
tart* with the mention.
docs/006-deployment.md covers the accounts, the `prepare` command template, upgrades and troubleshoo
ting; SETUP.md is the guided setup an agent can follow with you.
## Setup
Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:
> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.
It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures eve
rything. SETUP.md is what it follows.

## Fork notes / 本分支说明
This copy adds two changes on top of the upstream research prototype, for using it inside a shared D
SH profile with one GitHub account:
- **One account can request and act.** A message the agent's own account writes counts as that accou
nt's explicit request when it *starts* with `@<login>`; its other messages (acknowledgements, progre

ss, results) are still ignored, so the agent cannot trigger itself in a loop.
- **The worker environ
ment stays out of the host process.** `PATH`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` are appl
ied only for the setup check and restored at once. Installing the bundle into a profile you also use
for other Sessions no longer changes their git or `PATH`; worker sessions use the operator's own CL
I and git configuration, which one shared account makes equivalent.
### Shared-account mode
When the agent and the people asking share one GitHub account, mentioning yourself sends no notifica
tion, so the Source cannot rely on the account's notifications. Turn on **Receive new Issues** and *
*Receive comments in the repository** on the GitHub Source; it then reads the repository directly, a
nd a comment that starts with the agent's mention becomes an explicit request. Messages of that acco
unt that do not start with the mention are treated as the agent's own output and ignored, which keep
s acknowledgements and results from triggering new tickets.
## Development
`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.
